# awscc_backup_backup_access_point (Resource)

Creates a backup access point for an Amazon S3 recovery point. A backup access point provides on-demand, read-only access to the backup data in a recovery point through an Amazon S3 access point, without initiating a restore. While a backup access point is active for a recovery point, Backup pauses lifecycle transitions and blocks deletion of that recovery point.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `recovery_point_arn` (String) The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the recovery point for which to create the backup access point. The recovery point must be an Amazon S3 recovery point in the AVAILABLE, STOPPED, or COMPLETED state.

### Optional

- `access_point_in_time` (String) For continuous (point-in-time) recovery points, the timestamp in ISO 8601 format (for example 2021-11-27T03:30:27Z) that determines the point-in-time view of the backup data. The timestamp must be within the continuous backup's retention period at the time the access point is created. Do not specify this for snapshot recovery points. The service reports it back under AccessPointMetadata.
- `access_point_policy` (String) An optional resource-based policy document, in JSON, to apply to the underlying Amazon S3 access point. The policy controls how backup data can be accessed through the access point. If you do not specify a policy, access is governed by the caller's IAM permissions. The serialized policy may not exceed 200000 characters. This value is not returned by the service and cannot be updated in place.
- `name` (String) The name of the backup access point. This name is shared with the Amazon S3 access point namespace. It must be unique within your account and Region and cannot conflict with an existing Amazon S3 access point. If omitted, a name is generated.
- `tags` (Attributes List) The tags to assign to the backup access point. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tags))

### Read-Only

- `access_point_metadata` (Attributes) Metadata the service reports for the backup access point. Once the access point reaches the AVAILABLE status this carries the Amazon S3 access point ARN and alias; for continuous recovery points it also echoes the AccessPointInTime that was supplied at create time. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--access_point_metadata))
- `arn` (String) The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the backup access point.
- `backup_vault_arn` (String) The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the backup vault that contains the recovery point.
- `backup_vault_name` (String) The name of the backup vault that contains the recovery point.
- `creation_time` (String) The date and time that the backup access point was created.
- `id` (String) Uniquely identifies the resource.
- `resource_arn` (String) The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the resource that was backed up, such as an Amazon S3 bucket.
- `resource_type` (String) The type of Amazon Web Services resource associated with the recovery point. For example, S3 for Amazon Simple Storage Service.
- `status` (String) The current status of the backup access point.

<a id="nestedatt--tags"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tags`

Optional:

- `key` (String) The key name of the tag.
- `value` (String) The value for the tag.


<a id="nestedatt--access_point_metadata"></a>
### Nested Schema for `access_point_metadata`

Read-Only:

- `access_point_in_time` (String) For a continuous recovery point, the point in time the backup access point exposes, echoed back by the service as supplied at create time. Absent for snapshot recovery points. A plain string rather than a date-time, because it is one entry of the service's string-to-string metadata map.
- `s3_access_point_alias` (String) The alias of the Amazon S3 access point that Backup provisioned. Use this with standard Amazon S3 read APIs to access the backup data. Populated once the backup access point reaches the AVAILABLE status.
- `s3_access_point_arn` (String) The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Amazon S3 access point that Backup provisioned. Use this with standard Amazon S3 read APIs to access the backup data. Populated once the backup access point reaches the AVAILABLE status.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = awscc_backup_backup_access_point.example
  identity = {
    arn = "arn"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `arn` (String) The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the backup access point

#### Optional

- `account_id` (String) AWS Account where this resource is managed
- `region` (String) Region where this resource is managed

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = awscc_backup_backup_access_point.example
  id = "arn"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
$ terraform import awscc_backup_backup_access_point.example "arn"
```
